general.q: Which British seabird is often nicknamed the 'Sea Parrot' due to the distinctive appearance of its beak?
general.why: Atlantic puffins are famous for their brightly coloured beaks during the spring and summer breeding season.

general.q: Which is the largest island in the world that is not generally classified as a continent?
general.why: While Australia is larger, it is defined as a continent rather than an island, making Greenland the largest.

general.q: Who was the last British monarch to belong to the House of Hanover?
general.why: Victoria was succeeded by her son Edward VII, who belonged to his father's house, Saxe-Coburg and Gotha.

general.q: Which fruit is used as the base to produce the clear, cherry-flavoured brandy known as Kirsch?
general.why: Kirsch is a clear, colourless brandy traditionally made from the double distillation of morello cherries.

general.q: Which word for a scene of uproar and confusion derives from the name of a medieval London hospital?
general.why: Bedlam is a contraction of Bethlehem, the name of a hospital once used as a mental institution.

pop.q: In the sitcom Father Ted, what is the name of the fictional Craggy Island song entered into Eurosong 96?
pop.why: The music video features Ted and Dougal frolicking in a field with a horse.

pop.q: Which electronic music group's track 'Firestarter' featured on the soundtrack of the 1996 game Wipeout 2097?
pop.why: The game's high-octane soundtrack helped define the 'Cool Britannia' era of the PlayStation.

pop.q: In Monty Python and the Holy Grail, what detail must Bridge of Death victims know about a swallow?
pop.why: The bridge keeper asks about the bird's airspeed velocity, leading to this famous retort.

pop.q: Which collectible toy craze of the late 1990s featured beanbag animals with names like 'Patti the Platypus'?
pop.why: Launched in 1993, they became a global phenomenon with rare versions selling for thousands.

pop.q: Which food product's TV adverts featured metallic robotic Martians laughing at humans peeling potatoes?
pop.why: The iconic 1970s adverts featured robots laughing at the 'primitive' way humans made mashed potatoes.

music.q: Which guitarist rejoined the Red Hot Chili Peppers in 1998, six years after his first departure from the band?
music.why: Frusciante's return heralded a huge commercial peak for the band, including the album 'Californication'.

music.q: Which boy band kept Mariah Carey's 'All I Want for Christmas Is You' off the UK Number 1 spot in December 1994?
music.why: 'Stay Another Day' is the group's only Number 1 and remains a festive staple in the UK.

music.q: Which pop group won the Eurovision Song Contest for the UK in 1981 with the song 'Making Your Mind Up'?
music.why: The group's win became iconic thanks to a choreographed routine where the men ripped off the women's skirts.

music.q: Which 1985 album by Kate Bush became her second UK Number 1 and includes the hit 'Running Up That Hill'?
music.why: The album was self-produced and used the Fairlight CMI synthesiser to create its unique art-pop sound.

music.q: Which artist's music video for the 1986 hit 'Sledgehammer' is the most awarded in MTV Video Music Awards history?
music.why: The groundbreaking stop-motion video was created by Aardman Animations, the studio behind Wallace & Gromit.

mix.q: Who is the only constant member of the English rock band The Cure?
mix.why: Smith has been the lead singer and primary songwriter since the band formed in 1978.

mix.q: In which year did the Battle of Hastings take place?
mix.why: This pivotal battle marked the beginning of the Norman Conquest of England.

mix.q: In the sitcom Only Fools and Horses, what is the name of the pub frequented by Del Boy and Rodney?
mix.why: The Nag's Head was the Peckham local where most of the Trotters' deals were made.

mix.q: Which musician created the virtual band Gorillaz alongside artist Jamie Hewlett?
mix.why: Albarn formed the group in 1998 following his success with the Britpop band Blur.

mix.q: What is the highest mountain in the British Isles?
mix.why: Located in the Scottish Highlands, it stands at 1,345 metres above sea level.

mix.q: In the 1984 film Ghostbusters, what is the name of the giant marshmallow mascot?
mix.why: The Stay Puft Marshmallow Man was the chosen form of the Destructor, Gozer.

mix.q: Which planet in our solar system is known as the Red Planet?
mix.why: Iron oxide on its surface gives the planet its distinctive reddish appearance.

mix.q: Which Oasis album became the fastest-selling album in UK history upon its release in 1997?
mix.why: It sold over 696,000 copies in its first three days on sale.

mix.q: In the sci-fi sitcom Red Dwarf, what type of creature is the character Cat evolved from?
mix.why: The character evolved over three million years from Lister's pet cat, Frankenstein.

mix.q: In the Harry Potter series, what is the name of the station platform for the Hogwarts Express?
mix.why: It is hidden behind a brick wall at King's Cross Station in London.
